newsitem.title: USA: No bail for Michigan men held on kidnapping charges.
newsitem.headline: No bail for Michigan men held on kidnapping charges.

text.p: Two men accused of abducting Michigan sisters and driving them to Florida last month were ordered by a federal magistrate Friday to stay in jail without bond.

Ronald Stafford, 22, and Richard Geer, 20, did not enter a plea when they were brought before the U.S. District Court in Grand Rapids, where federal prosecutors read kidnapping charges against them, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Attorney's Office in Grand Rapids said.

Federal Magistrate Hugh Brenneman Jr. ordered that they continue to be held without bond. A proceeding for the third defendant, 17-year-old Lee Stafford, was held in the judge's chambers because he is a juvenile.
The trio also will face two Michigan kidnapping charges each for allegedly abducting Teresa and Jessica Hainer, ages 9 and 6, as they left their school bus near Kalamazoo, Michigan, March 21.
Authorities launched a nationwide manhunt and the girls were found four days later in Daytona, Florida.

Bob Pangle, chief assistant prosecutor of Kalamazoo County, said Friday state and federal prosecutors were continuing to review the case and will eventually only move forward with one set of charges. One issue to be resolved was whether to try the juvenile as an adult.
The federal kidnapping charges were more severe than the state statute, Pangle said, carrying a potential mandatory life sentence, depending on the aggravated nature of the crime.
